text:
## Creative brief
Plan a ~60-second documentary about how Viviana turned her pottery into Mud Witch and why she values pottery.

## Overview & Tone

This piece is cut as an intimate, character-driven profile that balances tactile studio craft with Viviana Matsuda’s playful, body-positive philosophy. Rather than a standard biographical overview, the edit leans into rhythm, contrast, and voice: starting cold to focus our attention on the earthy forms, pivoting into her vibrant studio world as the music enters, dropping audio for comedic and thematic punctuation, and finishing on a tender, warm resolution that lingers on her purpose as an artist.

---

## Story Beats

#### 1. Cold Open & Introduction (0:00–0:15) [node: beat_d6ce2559-f1ad-408b-ab68-11a21f9844bb]

We begin in absolute silence with no music [node: card_e066908d-9408-4b0f-95e5-1f8b4f0672cb], letting the viewer absorb the visual identity of the studio right away. The visual opens on a curated shelf display of pastel ceramics and tableware, trimmed down from B-roll reel B003C011_240719YX [node: card_101f8327-1834-4187-9442-d2083633d86b] (B003C011_240719YX (21.3s–37.9s)). Underneath this shot, Viviana’s voiceover introduces her signature vessels—explaining how she makes these curvy silhouettes like the "Chubby Mug" and "Venus mug" [node: card_e8fc5195-29a6-4e7d-8c13-496d34c10b42]—pulled from A-roll take A001C004_240718BC [node: card_f97eea56-f868-41f7-ac9c-300104a3e200] (A001C004_240718BC (693.9s–702.1s)) with the initial "and" cleanly trimmed off. 

Right as she says "shapes," we cut away to a brief two-beat visual breath [node: card_cbbe02aa-acf2-4f3d-998e-16a836b814bb], bridged by dynamic studio cutaway B003C050_240719XK [node: card_0e35dba9-6c40-4982-9d75-2c910e9c1239] (B003C050_240719XK (9.6s–14.2s)). This cutaway leads us directly into our first on-camera sync shot: Viviana introducing herself as a full-time potter and introducing the brand Mud Witch [node: card_40d2cd8a-a713-4bd1-89db-e6e73b66437c] using A001C002_240718OR [node: card_46454ac3-692b-4557-9aa3-23de46fdfdc0] (A001C002_240718OR (15.092717391304346s–25s)), tightened up by excising her hesitant opening "um." Exactly on this on-camera cut, the gentle piano of `calm_reflective` enters [node: card_a2731381-84f5-4506-a04d-3cabd6dfd37f] (projects/mudwitch-documentary/sound/calm_reflective.wav (real stock audio file — use directly, do not generate a replacement)) [node: card_7d6b5f6b-1697-4d55-9357-6d40ad9a6207]. Throughout this opening and the rest of the timeline, we establish our global mix rule: ducking the music bed by roughly 15 dB under dialogue with smooth 2-second ramp fades whenever Viviana speaks [node: card_98b3d523-0b88-476b-a6da-74986069309a].

#### 2. Mud Witch Origin & Body Positivity (0:15–0:45) [node: beat_0183d02e-cae7-434d-81c8-b8b19eac937b]

From her self-introduction, Viviana takes us into the thematic heart of Mud Witch, where learning pottery converged with the body positivity movement [node: card_6f506efa-3cb4-4a0f-94fc-92fb39a9f1ec]. Rather than letting an empty five-second dead space stall momentum [node: card_71e52264-ba47-4856-a5ce-cb7fdb0c2475], we ensure that any breathing room between dialogue lines is actively covered with evocative cutaways [node: card_a45bb05f-b29a-4e03-8205-851f988e1a47], carefully pairing visual assets to mirror the narrative concepts she describes [node: card_8ceed266-cf78-4388-90e1-cb56972e53dd].

She recounts experimenting with 11 natural clay bodies that reflected the full spectrum of skin tones [node: card_0f02f85c-f123-4284-a900-8279ba597bfc], taken from clip A001C004_240718BC [node: card_ea50fa32-f710-4a3d-854b-df161a945271] (A001C004_240718BC (728.5s–737.2s)). We trim her opening vocal tick but deliberately preserve her pause after "so they were like naked"—cutting the background music out cold for a beat [node: card_34312be9-1cce-4d01-a1f8-57bc34a81267] and supporting the moment visually with unglazed, naked bisque ware lined up on the studio shelves [node: card_701188d5-5db5-4fe0-8fb6-8863b239d68a]. 

After a beat of deadpan silence [node: card_c60cd760-bcc0-48c6-808e-6072f698c230], we cut immediately to her delivery: "And then I was like, well, let's slap some color on these, let's clothe these babes" [node: card_64845a8e-c69c-43f7-aac8-41d6492e5039] from take A001C004_240718BC [node: card_a3ebf6c1-748c-4538-823e-b95c7c0c89a4] (A001C004_240718BC (738.1s–742.4s)). The piano track re-enters instantly to reward the comedic timing [node: card_f69d1c67-0d9c-45ea-abe0-d65c5e46a1ae], layered under vivid B-roll of bright glaze and color being brushed onto raw ceramic pieces [node: card_28540d29-27da-4b34-9f02-c4609f5d911d]. 

Giving her speech a momentary breath [node: card_088c68f5-2ddf-4024-b33e-d74bb7be4c46], we dive into the core emotional thesis of her craft via clip A001C004_240718BC [node: card_39af0ccd-92fa-420c-8668-211b24050ef0] (A001C004_240718BC (668.9s–682.5s)). Here, we slice out the mid-sentence stammering with a clean jump cut disguised under process B-roll, preserving her strong opening and landing firmly on her resonant idea of "smushing things together" to celebrate diverse bodies.

#### 3. Resolution & Outro (0:45–1:00) [node: beat_6d3ff114-b367-428f-998d-66ba30b97ad6]

To resolve the narrative, we pivot from the technical making of pottery to Viviana's overarching purpose: bringing joy to people [node: card_c6f8d0fa-02dd-4094-ab4b-731a6e963d85]. We use her sincere on-camera delivery from A001C004_240718BC [node: card_4f921b97-b4b9-47bb-8652-009e0b417517] (A001C004_240718BC (897.6s–906.3s)) ("It started off as one thing, and now it's just like, I just want to make something that, like, makes people smile"), bypassing alternate interview take A001C004_240718BC [node: card_28ca20cd-7ce5-4b3b-b9e4-6020f9d8466f] (A001C004_240718BC (756s–762s)) to keep this ending clean, concise, and emotionally focused.

As her voice trails off, we cut away from the ceramic objects and keep our lens exclusively on Viviana [node: card_04d5a74e-f815-4786-8109-18494409b155]. We cut to B003C006_240719KM [node: card_f3e4191e-fa99-4e50-b833-cc9fd82b6d58] (B003C006_240719KM (131.5s–135s)) featuring her seated at a table surrounded by bright studio decor, re-timed down by 25% speed so her genuine smile lingers. We match this with dreamy, slow-motion footage of her painting in the studio [node: card_6407336a-229b-4fe2-99a2-91511c592b22], letting the visuals breathe as the sparse piano notes of `calm_reflective` ring out untethered for at least three seconds [node: card_c49460b6-097f-4320-805d-8624a215d3ce]. Finally, a clean graphic title card for Mud Witch appears [node: card_9396b8e4-659d-4c91-bf8e-88964b6b8a82], fading out smoothly over the final sustained chord.

## Constraints

- The plan above is the spec — it already made the editorial calls (what to use, what to omit, how to sequence and combine material). Follow the plan's own decisions rather than independently re-deriving them from first principles.
- Track is authoritative for whatever the plan places on a given track. A shot the plan describes as A-Roll must land on the A-Roll track, B-Roll on B-Roll, music on the Music track, and text/graphics on the Text/Graphics track. A card does not count as fulfilled merely because related material appears elsewhere in the timeline on the wrong track.
- Timecodes and durations in the plan are approximate targets, not exact requirements — use editorial judgment on the actual cut points, same as any real edit.
- A Music card whose source names a real file path (marked "real stock audio file") must be added directly with `edit-timeline add-clip <path> --row music --role music` — do not call `/generate music` for it.

## Instructions for tagging

When adding a clip with `edit-timeline add-clip`, attach the corresponding plan node ID using `--node-ids card_<id>` (or `beat_<id>` for a beat-level marker).

If one clip fulfills multiple plan node ids, include all applicable ones.

Only attach a node ID when the clip actually fulfills what the plan describes for it, including its named track. Use the exact node IDs from the plan. Do not invent or modify them.

## Completion requirements

Before finishing, verify against the plan's own decisions, not the original grid.

For each beat, confirm the edit the plan describes was actually realized: the right material landed on the right track, in the intended order, with any transitions/overlaps the plan called out.

For any node id the plan itself named as an intentionally unused alternative or backup, no further action is needed — that was already the plan's own decision, not something to silently reconsider or silently include anyway.

A node id that the plan actively describes using, but that never lands on the corresponding clip, is a real gap — note it and the reason in verification.
